findings.description: When the main checkout is detached, the new paused branch skips straight to the next loop iteration, so `sweepDeadTurns` (dead-turn resumes and the conductor nudge) and `findStalledSessions` (STALLED lines) never run. Neither one depends on the target branch, and at deb704d they still ran in this state.

If `armedGitDrivers` throws, `armed` becomes `["(driver check failed: X)"]`, so the message reads "was not put back because (driver check failed: X) is armed". That presents a read failure as an armed driver. Skipping the restore here is correct (it fails closed); the wording should say the driver check failed instead of "is armed".

The symref rethrow is chosen by `error.message.includes('symbolic ref')`, so a session that deletes the loose target ref and writes a packed-refs line containing 'symbolic ref' gets git's raw `Command failed: … rev-parse …` stderr, including its own packed-refs text, printed in place of the 'moved from X to nowhere' refusal. Nothing is checked out either way and control characters are stripped (by git and by the CLI catch at src/cli/index.ts:1696). A typed error class (as ArmedGitDriverError does) would make the match exact.

The new call-site comment 'nothing was scanned, and the stored overlaps and the beat were kept' repeats the explanation just written at the seam in src/core/overlap.service.ts:46-49 ('the stored overlaps and the beat are kept, and the caller can say the radar is paused'). general.md:130-132 (Seam-duplication test) says the explanation should live at the seam. Keep only the part that is specific to the caller, that `pup status` reads the radar as stale, or move the 'returns undefined' contract into scanOverlaps's JSDoc, which still describes an always-array return.

The paused branch copies the loop tail (`if (opts.once) return; Atomics.wait(...); continue;`) and keeps `'paused'` in the same `previous` slot as the JSON snapshot. Any later change to the wait or the snapshot format now has to be made in two places.
